lessons.title: Trigonometry and bearings
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Trigonometry: sine, cosine and tangent in right-angled triangles, angles of elevation and depression, three-figure bearings (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the O Level Mathematics syllabus; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Choose and use sine, cosine or tangent to find a side or an angle in a right-angled triangle.
Solve problems with angles of elevation and depression.
Use three-figure bearings and back bearings.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references are to be checked against the current Cameroon GCE Board O Level Mathematics syllabus (the sine and cosine rules may also be required; they are only mentioned here).
Rounding conventions (3 significant figures for lengths, 1 decimal place for angles) are common practice; check the instructions used on GCE papers.

blocks.title: The three ratios (SOH CAH TOA)
blocks.md:
In a right-angled triangle, for an acute angle θ:

- $\sin \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
- $\cos \theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$
- $\tan \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$

The **hypotenuse** is opposite the right angle; the **opposite** side faces θ; the **adjacent** side touches θ.

blocks.caption: The names of the sides depend on the angle θ.
blocks.alt: A right-angled triangle with the right angle at the bottom right. The angle theta is at the bottom left. The long sloping side is the hypotenuse, the vertical side is opposite theta and the horizontal side is adjacent to theta.

blocks.title: Three-figure bearings
blocks.md:
A **bearing** gives a direction as an angle measured **from north, clockwise**, written with **three figures**.

- North is 000°, east 090°, south 180°, west 270°.
- North-east is 045°, south-west is 225°.

blocks.caption: The bearing of B from A is 060°: start at the north line at A and turn clockwise.
blocks.alt: Point A with a vertical arrow labelled N pointing up. A second arrow goes from A up and to the right to point B. The angle of 60 degrees between the north arrow and AB is marked.

blocks.title: Back bearing
blocks.md:
The bearing of A from B differs from the bearing of B from A by 180°:

- add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°;
- subtract 180° if it is 180° or more.

Example: B from A is 060°, so A from B is 240°.

blocks.title: Method
blocks.md:
1. Draw a sketch; for bearings, draw a **north line** at each point.
2. Find a right-angled triangle and mark the known side and angle.
3. Name the sides (hyp, opp, adj) relative to the angle, then choose the ratio that links the known and the unknown.
4. Solve with the calculator **in degrees**, then round (lengths to 3 significant figures, angles to 1 decimal place).

blocks.title: Example 1: angle of elevation
blocks.statement: From a point on level ground 20 m from the foot of a palm tree, the angle of elevation of the top of the tree is 35°. Find the height h of the tree.

steps.md: Relative to the 35° angle, h is the **opposite** side and 20 m is the **adjacent** side: use tan.

blocks.title: Example 2: bearing and distance
blocks.statement: A boat sails 12 km from a port P on a bearing of 060° to a point Q. How far north and how far east of P is Q? What is the bearing of P from Q?

steps.md: The angle between the north line and PQ is 60°. The **north** distance is adjacent to this angle, so use cos:
The **east** distance is opposite the 60° angle, so use sin:
Back bearing: 060° is less than 180°, so the bearing of P from Q is 060° + 180° = 240°.

blocks.answer: **Q is 6 km north and about 10.4 km east of P; the bearing of P from Q is 240°.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Calculator in radians or grads instead of degrees: tan 35 then gives a wrong value.
- Measuring a bearing anticlockwise, or from east instead of north.
- Writing a bearing with two figures: 60° must be written 060°.
- Calling the longest side « opposite »: the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.
- Rounding in the middle of a calculation: keep full calculator values until the end.

items: For triangles without a right angle, the **sine rule** $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$ and the **cosine rule** $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc \cos A$ are used (check whether they are required in your syllabus).

exercises.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 10 cm long and one of the acute angles is 30°. Find the length of the side opposite the 30° angle, in cm.
mistakes: Using cos 30°: that gives the adjacent side (about 8.66 cm).
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: What is the three-figure bearing of due west?
exercises.explanation: Turning clockwise from north: east is 090°, south 180° and west 270°.
exercises.method: Picture the compass and turn clockwise from north.
mistakes: Choosing 090°: that is east (turning anticlockwise by mistake).
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite an angle θ is 3 cm and the adjacent side is 4 cm. Find θ in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
exercises.method: Opposite and adjacent: use tan, then the inverse function (shift tan) on the calculator.
mistakes: Computing tan 0.75 instead of the inverse tan of 0.75.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: The bearing of a village B from a village A is 125°. Find the bearing of A from B, in degrees.
exercises.explanation: 125° is less than 180°, so the back bearing is 125° + 180° = **305°**.
exercises.method: Draw north lines at A and B: the two angles are alternate angles, so the bearings differ by 180°.
mistakes: Answering 55° (180° − 125°): a back bearing differs by exactly 180°.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: From the top of a cliff 30 m high near Limbe, the angle of depression of a fishing boat is 25°. How far is the boat from the foot of the cliff? Give your answer in metres, to 3 significant figures.
exercises.explanation: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles), so at the boat the angle is 25°. The height 30 m is opposite and the distance d is adjacent: $\tan 25^\circ = \frac{30}{d}$, so $d = \frac{30}{\tan 25^\circ} \approx \frac{30}{0.4663} \approx 64.3$ m.
exercises.method: Draw the horizontal at the top of the cliff; the angle of depression is measured down from it.
mistakes: Computing 30 × tan 25° ≈ 14.0 m: the unknown is in the denominator.
Putting the 25° angle at the top of the cliff inside the triangle (the angle there is 65°).
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: A cyclist rides 8 km from town A due east to town B, then 6 km due south from B to town C.
exercises.method: East then south makes a right angle at B. Use Pythagoras for AC, tan for the angle at A, then add 90° to get the bearing.
mistakes: Giving 36.9° as the bearing: the bearing is measured from north, not from east.
Using sin or cos with a length you have rounded.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level Paper 2 style

parts.prompt: Find the direct distance AC, in km.
parts.explanation: The angle at B is 90°: $AC^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 = 64 + 36 = 100$, so AC = 10 km.

parts.prompt: Find the angle BAC in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
Find the bearing of C from A, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.explanation: AB points due east (090°). C is a further 36.9° clockwise from AB, so the bearing is 90° + 36.9° = **126.9°**.

exercises.prompt: A hunter walks 7 km due north from a village P to a point Q. He then walks due east from Q to a point R. The bearing of R from P is 040°.
exercises.method: The angle QPR is 40° and the angle at Q is 90°. PQ is adjacent to the 40° angle.
mistakes: Using sin 40° for QR: QR is opposite and PQ is adjacent, so use tan.
Answering 040° or 140° for the back bearing.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level Paper 2 style

parts.prompt: Calculate the distance QR, in km, correct to 2 decimal places.
Calculate the distance PR, in km, correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the bearing of P from R, in degrees.

exercises.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, what is $\sin \theta$ equal to?
How is a three-figure bearing measured?
exercises.explanation: Bearings always start from the north line and turn clockwise.

exercises.prompt: What is the three-figure bearing of south-east?
exercises.explanation: South-east is halfway between east (090°) and south (180°): 135°.

exercises.prompt: What is the exact value of $\cos 60^\circ$?
Which side of a right-angled triangle is the hypotenuse?
choices: The side opposite the right angle
The side opposite the angle θ
The side next to the angle θ
exercises.explanation: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle; it is always the longest side.
